patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Fastmail and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits. Choose Fastmail only if your buying job matches “Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addre” rather than OpenPhone's shape. Choose OpenPhone only if your buying job matches “Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI —” rather than Fastmail's shape. Workflow advantage: Fastmail leans shared coverage; OpenPhone leans business-phone, sales-calling. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Fastmail and OpenPhone share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Fastmail is Privacy-focused business email, calendar and contacts with custom domains and shared addresses — Business Basic from $3/user/month annual; a; OpenPhone is Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and Sona AI — Starter from $15/user/month annual..
- Company-size focus: Fastmail (micro, small-business) vs OpenPhone (solo, small-business, mid-market).
- Workflow coverage skew: Fastmail-leaning — vs OpenPhone-leaning business-phone, sales-calling.
- Researched limits: Fastmail — Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; OpenPhone — US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story.

Limitations — Fastmail: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications; Shared addresses, shared calendars and the shared address book require Standard or above; OpenPhone: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story; Phone menus, automatic recording and deeper CRM require Business or above.

Poor-fit cases: Fastmail is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Not a business phone, WhatsApp or team-chat product — adjacent to business communications · OpenPhone is a poor fit when that limitation bites: US/Canada-centric calling footprint — not a global UCaaS carrier story · Avoid Fastmail if you actually need OpenPhone's motion (Modern SMB shared business phone (also branded Quo) with shared numbers, SMS and)
